chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Al-Lu'lu'i, Hasan ibn Husayn, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Burayd Al-Ajli, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to throw the pebbles at the middle pillar on the second day. He said: 'Let him throw it on the third day for what missed him and for what is obligatory upon him on his day.' I said: 'And if he does not remember except on the day of departure (Yawm al-Nafar)?' He said: 'Let him throw it and there is nothing upon him.' (Note: The text continues with a separate ruling regarding the sick, fearful, shepherds, and slaves being permitted to throw at night, which is included in the body as it is part of the same narrational context in this specific text segment).
And permission has been granted for the sick, the fearful, the shepherds, and the slaves to throw (the pebbles) at night. (He) narrated.

key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّفْرِ: The day of departure (13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets to throw the Jamarah on the second day of Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *Nasi* (forgetfulness) in Hajj rituals, specifically regarding the middle Jamarah on the 11th of Dhu al-Hijjah. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the missed stone is combined with the current day's obligation on the 12th, demonstrating the principle of ease (*Taysir*) in ritual duties. The narration further extends this concession to specific groups like the sick and fearful, allowing night throwing, which aligns with the Quranic allowance for those who fear hardship.
